title: Records, enums and exceptions

notes: The enum gives four named choices the compiler can check.
The record gets a constructor, properties, == and ToString for free.
`with` makes a changed copy; start is still (0, 0).
The switch ends with a throw for any value that isn't one of the four.
The custom exception carries a clear message; finally runs either way.

exercises.title: Moving on a grid
exercises.prompt:
Direction and the record GridPos are started for you. Finish:
- GridPos.Move(Direction d, int steps = 1): a NEW position moved that many steps (North is Y + steps, South is Y - steps, East is X + steps, West is X - steps). Use `with`. Any other Direction value throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.
- GridPos.DistanceTo(GridPos other): grid distance |dx| + |dy|.
- Compass.TurnRight(Direction d): North -> East -> South -> West -> North.

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var a = new GridPos(3, 3); var b = a.Move(Direction.South, 2); return a + " " + b.Y; }))()
tests.name: the original doesn't change
a value that isn't a direction

tests.why: Make the moved copy with a `with` expression.

hints: public GridPos Move(Direction d, int steps = 1) => d switch { Direction.North => this with { Y = Y + steps }, ... };
End the switch with _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(d))

exercises.title: Weather advice
exercises.prompt:
The enum Weather is given. In static class FarmAdvice:
- string Advice(Weather w) with a switch expression: Sunny "Good day to harvest", Rainy "Plant the beans", Stormy "Stay inside and check the drains", Dry "Water the seedlings early". Any other value throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.
- Weather Parse(string text): turns text like "  stormy " or "DRY" into a Weather (ignore case and spaces). Anything that isn't one of the four names, including numbers like "7" and null, throws ArgumentException.
hints: Advice: return w switch { Weather.Sunny => "...", ..., _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(w)) };
Parse: if (text != null && Enum.TryParse(text.Trim(), true, out Weather w) && Enum.IsDefined(w)) return w;
After that if, throw new ArgumentException($"Unknown weather: {text}");

exercises.title: A savings group account
exercises.prompt:
1. Write InsufficientFundsException : Exception with a decimal Shortfall property, constructor InsufficientFundsException(decimal shortfall), and a message.
2. Fix SavingsAccount: Deposit and Withdraw throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException for amounts of 0 or less; Withdraw of more than the Balance throws InsufficientFundsException(amount - Balance) and leaves the balance alone.
3. Teller.TryWithdraw(account, amount): use try/catch/finally. Return "OK, balance {Balance}" on success, "Short by {Shortfall}" for not enough money, "Bad amount" for a bad amount. In finally, add 1 to Teller.Attempts (every call counts).

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var a = new SavingsAccount("Wanjiru", 500); a.Withdraw(200); a.Deposit(50); return a.Balance.ToString(); }))()
tests.name: normal use

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var a = new SavingsAccount("Juma", 100); a.Withdraw(250); return "no error"; }))()
tests.name: too much

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var a = new SavingsAccount("Juma", 100); try { a.Withdraw(250); } catch (InsufficientFundsException e) { return e.Shortfall + " " + a.Balance; } return "no throw"; }))()
tests.name: the shortfall, balance untouched

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { int before = Teller.Attempts; var a = new SavingsAccount("A", 50); string r1 = Teller.TryWithdraw(a, 80); string r2 = Teller.TryWithdraw(a, -5); return r1 + " | " + r2 + " | " + (Teller.Attempts - before); }))()
tests.name: teller failures still count

tests.why: Count the attempt in a finally block.

hints: public class InsufficientFundsException : Exception { public decimal Shortfall { get; } public InsufficientFundsException(decimal shortfall) : base("...") { Shortfall = shortfall; } }
Withdraw: check amount <= 0 first, then if (amount > Balance) throw new InsufficientFundsException(amount - Balance);
TryWithdraw: try { ...; return ...; } catch (InsufficientFundsException ex) { ... } catch (ArgumentOutOfRangeException) { ... } finally { Attempts++; }

quiz.q: record GridPos(int X, int Y). new GridPos(1, 2) == new GridPos(1, 2) is…
quiz.why: Value equality is the point of records.

quiz.q: What does pos with { Y = 9 } do?
choices: Makes a copy with Y = 9; pos is unchanged

quiz.q: Why end an enum switch with _ => throw ...?
choices: Because (Direction)9 compiles, and you want a loud error, not silent nonsense
quiz.why: Any int can be cast to an enum.

quiz.q: Which catch block is the problem? try { ... } catch (Exception) { }
choices: It silently swallows every error, including real bugs
quiz.why: Catch only what you can handle.

quiz.q: Player or GridPos: which should be a record?
quiz.why: Records for values; classes for things with identity that change.
